approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds molecular graphs by connected-fragment crossover and ordinary mutation from a bounded high-scoring population; direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled. It retains every accepted score in a task-local archive and fits a Gaussian process using radius-two, chirality-aware Morgan environment counts folded into 2,048 coordinates. Generalized count-Tanimoto similarity supplies the training and joint pool covariance. Fixed noise and archive score normalization define the fitted posterior. Each batch selects available maxima from correlated posterior function draws over a larger pool of fresh valid unique offspring. Accepted feedback updates the archive and score-greedy survivors.
approach.novelty: Remove only the final folding of environment identifiers into 2,048 bins. Keep the same local environments and their occurrence counts, but align them by the native environment hash identifiers when calculating the same count-Tanimoto kernel. This separates distinct identifiers that previously shared a modulo bin and can change similarity weights, posterior means and covariance, then the identities selected by the existing allocator. Unlike the count-removal sibling, multiplicity remains; unlike the failed residual-scaling variant, allocation amplitude is unchanged. This does not make fingerprints unique: finite native hashes and identical local-environment multisets still alias. The current audit exposes kernel and choice changes without establishing endpoint benefit.

observed_bottleneck: The Parent n-62daf219c70a mixes distinct native Morgan identifiers into fixed-width count bins. Its complete current-profile mean endpoint is 0.5956696497334577, with seed population SD 0.02659287062806747. A new read-only audit of its 435 archived pools finds within-molecule modulo-bin mixing in 37950/69600 pool occurrences, with 59443 excess native identifiers beyond the occupied bins; training occurrences have 35193/65250 such exposures and 54864 excess identifiers. Native counts reproduce the original folded counts exactly after modulo-2048 summation, with no multiplicity-total mismatch. The fixed-data unfolded reference changes all 435 pool kernels and pool posteriors; 69562/69600 means and SDs differ above 1e-12, and the original correlated normals yield 388 changed batch sets and 1088 changed ordered choices. These are passive controls on actual Parent histories, not Child outcomes or scores of unselected alternatives. There are zero exactly folded-count-equivalent pairs within these current pools, so this evidence identifies similarity reweighting, not observed tie splitting. Historical n-559d25e9c9c7 instead had 41756 collision-exposed pool occurrences and 71752 excess identifiers under its exchange-containing conditions; its sole exact binary/count tie also remains native-hash-count-equivalent in the new passive check. Historical n-559d25e9c9c7 and n-98e8cdf5c51d reproduce the same trajectories and are not independent confirmations. Current multiplicity removal n-e00db808bbb4 loses 0.051295849138213355, supporting retained counts with task-seed exceptions. Current residual scaling n-38bcd7569cce raises selected-stream interval coverage yet loses 0.03814118675118202 on the complete endpoint panel, with all seed macros falling and eight task-seed gains. Neither count utility nor diagnostic improvement proves that folding is harmful or that its removal improves endpoints.
hypothesis: Replace fixed-width folded Morgan count coordinates with occurrence counts keyed by the corresponding native unfolded environment hash identifiers, using the same generalized count-Tanimoto covariance so distinct modulo-bin aliases no longer mix in posterior similarities.

finding_summary.headline: Unfolding changes covariance and selection but lowers every seed’s macro score
finding_summary.insights: The experiment rules out insufficient representation or allocation exposure as an explanation for the missing gain. Removing folding changes ordinary similarity relationships and adaptive choices, but it does not reliably help the retained optimizer. On the same Child selected molecules, prediction MSE improves only slightly, from 0.007847 to 0.007808, and interval coverage rises from 75.36% to 75.82%; those diagnostics do not rescue the endpoint result. All three median_2 streams worsen in prediction MSE while improving at the endpoint, further limiting a simple prediction-to-search explanation. Exact native-count ties remain, as do finite-hash and local-environment limits. The molecular output retains useful aromatic, amine, urea and carbonyl organization alongside reactive bonds, crowded rings and unspecified stereochemistry; neither the losses nor the median_2 gains establish a universal size or chemical-feasibility rule. This is a negative result for the incremental unfolding variant on this composition, not a reversal of the earlier evidence for retaining occurrence counts. Changed means and covariance, adaptive graph paths and possible lost accidental regularization remain unresolved mediators.
finding_summary.results: Native counts preserve multiplicity and remove modulo-bin mixing on 41,278 of 69,600 pool occurrences. All 435 pool kernels change against their folded controls, changing 392 selected sets while 43 sets remain identical. Nine distinct-molecule pairs still share native count vectors. Every active fit and choice reconstructs, and every evaluation completes. Mean endpoint score falls from 0.595670 to 0.547507, a decrease of 0.048163 rather than the required 0.002 increase. Seed macro changes are -0.077453, -0.013541 and -0.053495. Six task-seed endpoints improve and nine decline; all three median_2 endpoints improve. Macro dispersion drops from 0.026593 to 0.000322 around the lower mean.

molecular.headline: Aryl ureas, nitrogen/carbonyl rings and sulfur-rich amines coexist with oversized heterocycles, acyl halides and uncertain geometry
molecular.overall_character: All fifteen Child trajectories and fifteen published Parent trajectories named by the immutable brief were read: 4,500 observations per node, including 4,350 optimizer proposals per node. All five tasks and Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 are covered; no listed path is missing. The brief reports complete, profile-matched pairing to n-62daf219c70a at 300 observations per task and ten-member batches under the Research in Depth profile. The generated chemistry includes compact halogen-free aryl ureas, N-amino indole-like carbonyl systems, small unsaturated carbocycles, repeated azaheterocyclic carbonyl assemblies, imine-rich azaarenes, aryl amines carrying unusual sulfur environments, biphenyl or quinoline-linked nitrogen/dicarbonyl rings, and fluorinated imino/carbonyl heterocycles. Molecular size and chemical character vary markedly across seeds. Rings and aromatic-labelled atoms are abundant: proposal ring-digit incidence ranges from 0.9621 to 0.9862 and aromatic-string incidence from 0.9586 to 0.9816. Those are string-level readings, not demonstrations of stable aromaticity, feasible conformations or independent scaffold coverage. Structural diversity is moderate across the panel, with recurring leading series within seeds; the familiar urea, amide, lactam and amine groups rule out an absence of medicinal chemistry, while reactive acyl halides, unusual sulfur bonding and crowded ring topology make overall plausibility questionable and drug-likeness weak. Every task has stereocentre-string and charge-string incidence 0.0. Basic amines nevertheless occur, and potentially stereogenic ring centres remain unspecified. Sizes below are heavy-atom-token counts from the supplied SMILES. Only evaluated output is assessed: these trajectories cannot establish unselected-pool exposure or the chemical alternatives a pool contained. The stated folded-bin alias-removal intervention is distinct from native-hash or count-vector equivalence; native Morgan identifiers or equal count vectors do not certify molecular identity, and this report does not measure those equivalences. Equal scores likewise do not identify shared fingerprints. Chemical and paired-score associations below do not establish component activation or attribution. The reproducible read-only audit records all trajectory hashes, row counts and digest-extrema checks.

per_task.generated_character: The three seed leaders contain 24, 23 and 25 heavy-atom tokens. Seed 0 produces an N-amino indole-like bicyclic arene with methoxy, vinyl, chloromethyl and benzoyl substituents. Seed 1 instead reaches a halogen-free bridged aryl/unsaturated nitrogen ring bearing a methoxy group and an N-pyridyl urea. A tied 23-atom relative moves the oxygen into the ring connectivity. These leaders use recognizable carbonyl/urea chemistry, although their bridge geometry is not established. Seed 2 uses a benzene-fused four-membered unsaturated carbocycle carrying an anilide, methoxy and methylamino groups, plus a ketenimine side chain. Thus aromatic and polar functionality is present, but some connectivity is much less conventional than the initial indole carboxanilide. Mean proposal SMILES length is 41.1, halogen-string incidence 0.6701 and cumulated-double-bond incidence 0.0333. The high-scoring halogen-free seed-1 series is a substantive counterexample to universal halogen dependence.
liabilities: N-amino aromatic nitrogens, chloromethyl substituents and occasional N-F amides introduce context-specific reactivity concerns.
The benzene-fused four-membered unsaturated ring and ketenimine side chain raise geometric and stability concerns; their presence is not justified by SMILES validity alone.
The recognizable urea functionality does not by itself establish the feasibility or stereochemistry of its bridged core.
missing_features: The favorable aryl/polar organization is present, but consistently accessible alternatives to the bridged and small unsaturated ring connectivities are not established at the leading scores.
Specified stereochemical identity is missing in the saturated bridge environment, and the ketenimine-containing series lacks demonstrated geometric and stability characterization.

Local bond environments are not controlled consistently: the scored nonfluorinated amide counterpart and halogen-free urea show that direct N-halogen chemistry is not necessary throughout this output.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial indole carboxanilide scores 0.3051048083696145; the three seed leaders score 0.4254027310763201, 0.46746448265590934 and 0.40826532672592236. Isolated Br scores 0.0. Useful scores associate with retained aromatic/carbonyl organization, not halogen presence alone. Local comparisons are conditional: removing an amide N-F bond changes 0.4038761425223417 to 0.40650757542526167. In one seed-2 series, anilide-to-aryl-thioester replacement lowers 0.40196779766986834 to 0.3250152096349864; in a related N-amino-substituted series, the corresponding replacement raises 0.3900685872822928 to 0.40497388700123543. Neither amide nor thioester is universally favored. The two different seed-1 oxygen placements both score 0.46746448265590934, which does not establish fingerprint equivalence. Matched Parent endpoints are 0.39405142067435733, 0.47411701813450596 and 0.438972502037081. Seed 0 improves while seeds 1 and 2 decrease; the Child's compact halogen-free urea remains a chemical counterexample to treating all strong output as reactive halogen chemistry. No exact absent target motif is identifiable from these observations.

per_task.generated_character: The three seed leaders contain 44, 63 and 34 heavy-atom tokens. Seed 0 joins two carbonyl-rich nitrogen rings through an N-N bond and carries exocyclic unsaturation, an azaaromatic fragment, an aldehyde-containing side chain, and both an acyl chloride and an acyl fluoride. A tied relative replaces the acyl chloride with an acyl bromide. These are reactive acyl halides, not ordinary carbon-bound aryl halogens. Seed 1 is a large repeated azaheterocyclic carbonyl/oxygen-ring assembly with carbonate esters, allyloxy substitution, a nitrile-containing cumulated chain and a small fused oxygen-containing ring. Seed 2 instead links multiple azaarenes through imine/amidine-like segments and includes an N-chlorinated imino terminus with carbon-bound chlorine. Mean proposal SMILES length is 81.5, aromatic-string incidence 0.9690 and ring-digit incidence 0.9690. The set is ring-rich and often substantially elaborated; stable, compact heteroaromatic chemistry is not the dominant appearance of these particular leaders.
liabilities: Acyl chloride, bromide and fluoride groups, N-N connectivity, conjugated aldehyde-containing chains and N-chlorinated imines create substantial stability and handling questions.
Large repeated heterocyclic units and multiple ester/carbonate or imine linkages increase structural and synthetic complexity without a uniform score advantage.
Cumulated unsaturation and small fused rings require geometric assessment; lowercase aromatic notation does not resolve it.
missing_features: The output does not demonstrate consistently stable replacements for acyl halides, N-chlorinated imines and other reactive decorations while preserving the favorable heteroaromatic organization.
Compact, chemically independent alternatives to repeated heterocyclic assemblies remain limited among the evaluated leading series; this is not a statement about unselected pools.
Feasible geometry and defined stereochemical or imine configurations are not demonstrated for the fused and highly unsaturated assemblies.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted fused dione scores 0.548381482770623. An early peroxide-substituted quinoline scores 0.5100965759438103, while isolated Br scores the observed floor of 0.5. The three leaders reach 0.6235001463271876, 0.6170880178893099 and 0.6205348735011614. In the seed-0 leader, acyl chloride-to-bromide substitution leaves 0.6235001463271876 unchanged; this does not establish molecular or fingerprint equivalence and supplies no evidence that either reactive group is synthetically desirable. A ring-opened 44-atom final relative scores 0.5832761524546192, so atom count alone does not preserve reward. The seed-2 50-atom elaborated relative scores 0.619688253850436, below its 34-atom leader. Parent endpoints are 0.8561477222467935, 0.6248206599713055 and 0.6178024026512013, with 30-, 32- and 37-atom leaders. The Child loses in seeds 0 and 1 despite substantial enlargement; seed 2 improves with a smaller leader in a different imine-rich family. The Parent's stronger seed-0 thione/O-F/halomethyl family also had liabilities, so lower Child score cannot be read as either improved or worsened makeability in isolation.

per_task.generated_character: The three seed leaders contain 31, 27 and 30 heavy-atom tokens. Seed 0 links a halophenol/imine region through an aminoalkyl chain to an unusual ring-bound sulfur centre with S=O, S=C and S-N connections, and also carries a chloroalkyl side chain. Seed 1 has two substituted aryl regions, a saturated cyclic diamine, phenol/methoxy groups and a sulfur centre double-bonded to an exocyclic methylene while also attached to aryl carbon and nitrogen. These sulfur environments are not ordinary sulfonamides. Seed 2 joins a chloropyrrole and a small saturated nitrogen ring to a tertiary amine and fluorinated, chlorinated tetralin-like region; its ring nitrogen bears a terminal sulfur group written N[SH]=O. A close leading family uses bridged cyclic sulfur-oxide connectivity instead. Available aliphatic amines are clearly present throughout these leaders. Mean proposal SMILES length is 60.9 and halogen-string incidence 0.9897. Aryl amine organization is recognizable, but unusual sulfur bonding and connected ring geometry weaken confidence in ordinary medicinal-chemistry plausibility.
liabilities: S=C/S=O/S-N combinations and terminal hydrogen-bearing sulfur-oxide groups require environment-specific valence and stability scrutiny.
Small nitrogen rings, multiply connected sulfur-containing rings and unspecified saturated stereocentres raise synthesis and geometry questions.
Chloroalkyl groups, aryl halides and sizable aromatic surfaces coexist, but the trajectory scores do not characterize stability, solubility or selectivity.
missing_features: Conventional bond environments are not consistently maintained around sulfur while successful aryl/amine relationships are explored; strong sulfur-free relatives show that sulfur is not an indispensable universal component.
Explicit stereochemistry and conformational identity are absent for substituted tetralin-like centres, saturated nitrogen rings and bridged junctions.
The neutral SMILES do not resolve protonation states, although potentially basic centres are abundant; the records do not justify simply adding another amine.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: An N-sulfonyl cyclic amine scores 0.00021169315013374197; an early amide/carboxylate/sulfonamide assembly scores 0.0006269216484658979. The three seed leaders reach 0.9410969690840454, 0.9209804791284083 and 0.9766949967449473. Available aliphatic amines together with aromatic regions associate with higher scores, but this is not a nitrogen-count or sulfur requirement: a sulfur-free seed-0 aryl/amine assembly scores only 0.24375714718505176, whereas sulfur-free seed-2 carbonyl and hydroxylamine-substituted bridged variants score 0.9487092468687838 and 0.96818782227592. Their differing structures preclude attributing the values to sulfur removal alone. The sulfur-oxide bridged relative scores 0.9723252692687101. All three matched Parent endpoints are higher, at 0.9999989177995104, 0.9969753164881906 and 0.9999934235240012, in flexible or cyclic aryl-amine families; the Parent includes high-scoring ordinary sulfur-free amines. The observed gradient therefore supports functional-group presentation in context, not a need for unusual sulfur valence. These oracle values do not establish binding selectivity or physical accessibility.

per_task.generated_character: All three seed leaders contain 33 heavy-atom tokens. Seed 0 attaches an ethoxy/methyl biphenyl to a bridged nitrogen/dicarbonyl system with an enolic hydroxyl and an N-N ring closure. Seed 1 uses a propyl/ethoxy biphenyl attached to a partially unsaturated fused nitrogen/dicarbonyl ring system containing N-methyl lactam groups and a saturated amine. This seed-1 family is a comparatively recognizable combination of ordinary aryl, amide and amine chemistry. Seed 2 combines a propylquinoline, a pyrrole and an aminomethyl-linked bridged dicarbonyl/tertiary-amine ring. The Parent leaders contain 34, 32 and 29 atoms, so Child size change is not uniform. Proposal aromatic-string incidence is 0.9816, ring-digit incidence 0.9862 and mean SMILES length 56.4; halogen-string incidence is only 0.1184. These families supply a useful counterexample to the heavily halogenated output elsewhere. Geometry and stereochemical definition remain concerns, but not every leading ring system is equally exotic.
liabilities: The seed-0 N-N ring closure and enolic representation require local stability and tautomer assessment.
Bridged and partially unsaturated nitrogen/carbonyl rings can be synthetically demanding; higher score does not validate their routes or conformations.
Strong scores occur without substantial halogen decoration, so halogenation is not a general missing capability in these families.
missing_features: Stereochemical and conformational identity of the saturated bridges and ring junctions remains unresolved.

The favored aromatic/nitrogen/carbonyl organization is present, but consistent access to simpler feasible connectivities at the same leading scores is not established; the near-leading contracted ring is a useful partial counterexample.
Independent plausible evaluated alternatives within each leading family are limited, although the different biphenyl and quinoline/pyrrole families prevent a claim of global scaffold collapse.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted fused dione scores 0.1678386594791329. A 15-atom nitrogen/dicarbonyl ring lacking the larger aromatic region scores 0.08411963849598328; the final 21-atom quinoline/pyrrole product lacking the leader's nitrogen/carbonyl appendage scores 0.16922282244532988. A 56-atom duplicated heterocyclic assembly scores 0.11780871699819487 and ethene scores 0.0. Together these examples associate useful reward with combined aromatic and polar-ring context rather than simple growth, fragmentation or either region alone. The three leaders reach 0.23115033995213558, 0.24300288424853 and 0.22923668265172575, each above the matched Parent endpoint of 0.2258403994203931, 0.2214095461892601 and 0.22600312875247064. This all-seed gain must be preserved despite chemical concerns elsewhere. Deleting a ring nitrogen and contracting the seed-1 leader's ring gives a 32-atom relative scoring 0.24150836237182322, showing that the precise larger nitrogen ring is not uniquely necessary for a similar score. The record does not reveal a single missing target motif or a universal requirement for further ring elaboration.

per_task.generated_character: The three seed leaders contain 28, 27 and 25 heavy-atom tokens. Seed 0 has a fused imino/carbonyl nitrogen heterocycle carrying N-methyl and N-F groups, a fluoroethyl substituent and a fluorinated aryl fluoromethyl ester. That ester contains O-C-F connectivity, not an O-F bond. Seed 1 uses a large aromatic-labelled nitrogen/dicarbonyl ring bearing N-F, an enolic fluorinated cyclopentadiene and a fluorinated cyclohexadiene substituent. Its aromatic notation does not establish a stable planar aromatic ring. Seed 2 makes a multiply connected aryl/nitrogen heterocycle with two imino groups, a saturated fluorinated ring centre and an aryl acyl fluoride; the latter is C(=O)F, chemically distinct from fluoroalkyl substitution. Mean proposal SMILES length is 49.3. Aromatic-string and ring-digit incidences are 0.9586 and 0.9621, while cumulated-double-bond incidence is only 0.0011. The current leaders do not require the small cyclic cumulene seen in the Parent seed-2 leader, but other geometric and bond-environment liabilities remain.
liabilities: Direct N-F bonds and acyl fluoride functionality create different stability concerns; carbon-bound fluorine and O-C-F ester connectivity must not be conflated with them.
Large aromatic-labelled nitrogen rings, crowded fused/bridged connectivity and fluorinated enolic carbocycles require physical geometry and tautomer assessment.
More elaborate duplicated heterocycles can lose useful molecular context, while absence of a cyclic cumulene does not establish that a replacement topology is feasible.
missing_features: Stable bond environments and credible ring geometry are not consistently combined with the favorable compact fluorinated/polar organization.
Explicit saturated-centre and alkene stereochemistry, together with established enol/imino tautomeric identity, is missing from the cited representations.

The evaluated series do not establish stable local replacements for acyl fluoride or N-F at their exact leading scores; near-leading N-F-free chemistry and opposite local score responses require context-sensitive interpretation.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted fused dione scores 0.0020944534688323298; a 48-atom highly connected duplicated heterocycle scores 1.3307726692355508e-17 and isolated F scores 1.1043196211273875e-26. The three leaders reach 0.5186463461539925, 0.4880863339901072 and 0.5014496282827379. Reward associates with compact fluorinated/polar organization, not fluorine count or heterocycle multiplication alone. Moving one fluorine between the aryl and fused-ring regions in the seed-0 leading family changes 0.5186463461539925 to 0.5011774408284522. In other close seed-0 comparisons, an N-F-to-N-methyl change lowers 0.46148604570485713 to 0.3534091128637756, and replacing fluoromethyl ester with methyl ester lowers 0.4326345826918735 to 0.30121868572054644. These local counterexamples limit any claim that removing a reactive or fluorinated group always helps. Conversely, a differently connected seed-1 relative without direct N-F scores 0.4836905232399345, close to its seed leader; it is not an isolated N-F comparison. Parent endpoints are 0.6510211907030741, 0.4870057305679067 and 0.7208853668418119. The small seed-1 gain coexists with decreases in seeds 0 and 2, whose Parent families also had unresolved geometry or N-F liabilities. No exact absent pharmacophore can be inferred from these records.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This gap originates in the n-c55c3d520a2c assessment reproduced by n-62daf219c70a and is newly observed in n-b14daceabbeb on Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 at 300 observations per task and batches of ten. Current leading families include acyl halides, direct N-F, N-chlorinated imines and unusual S=C/S=O/S-N environments. Counterexamples are essential: a halogen-free urea scores 0.46746448265590934; removal of amide N-F changes 0.4038761425223417 to 0.40650757542526167; and a sulfur-free bridged amine scores 0.96818782227592. In another context N-F-to-N-methyl replacement lowers 0.46148604570485713 to 0.3534091128637756. These are conditional chemical associations, not uniform substitution rules or attribution to the covariance change.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve conventional local bond environments within otherwise useful aromatic and polar frameworks.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Offer conventional local alternatives that preserve favorable functional-group organization learned from accepted task-local feedback, distinguishing acyl halides, heteroatom-bound halogens and ordinary carbon-bound halogens. Treat sulfur by its full bond environment. The missing capability is reliable chemical context control, not a universal element ban or proof that a plausibility filter raises objective scores.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The geometry gap is inherited from n-c55c3d520a2c through n-62daf219c70a and recurs in this complete matched panel as benzene-fused small unsaturated rings, crowded aryl bridges, large aromatic-labelled nitrogen rings and imine-rich or cumulated side chains. High ring-digit and aromatic-string incidence do not establish stable conformations. The current leaders need not reproduce the Parent's cyclic-cumulene motif, and comparatively conventional urea and fused amide/amine families also score well. All three aromatic/nitrogen/dicarbonyl families improve over their matched Parent endpoints, so elaboration or ring formation is not uniformly score-worsening.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not reliably combine representable ring connectivity with demonstrably credible geometry and unsaturation patterns.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring transformations need attention to ring size, bridge connections, unsaturation and geometric compatibility, while maintaining access to ordinary fused and saturated ring chemistry. Assess feasible alternative connectivities using task-local feedback. Neither string validity nor a high score resolves this limitation, and the evidence does not support banning ring formation or assigning the issue to folded versus native hash representation.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This identity gap was recorded for n-c55c3d520a2c and reproduced by n-62daf219c70a; it persists in the current supplied three-seed panel. Every task's stereocentre-string incidence is 0.0, despite bridged urea cores, substituted nitrogen rings and fluorinated saturated centres in the cited leaders. Charge-string incidence is also 0.0, but available amines are present. The data establish unspecified identity, not a measured stereochemical or protonation-related score penalty.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator leaves potentially stereogenic saturated centres and ring junctions without specified stereochemical identity.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve or explicitly resolve stereochemistry where generated constitution requires it, with appropriate exceptions for achiral and configurationally unstable structures. Treat protonation, alkene geometry and tautomer identity separately. No particular stereoisomer, charge state or objective-specific structure is justified by these scores, and the chemical gap is not evidence of native-hash uniqueness or equivalence.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This gap is inherited from n-c55c3d520a2c via n-62daf219c70a and has new evaluated-output evidence in the current matched panel. Tiny late hydrocarbon/halogen products reach observed floors; some large duplicated heterocycles score far below compact leading frameworks. One 63-atom repeated heterocyclic leader remains below its 32-atom matched Parent leader, while a 34-atom alternative exceeds its 37-atom Parent. Counterexamples prevent a size rule: the three nitrogen/dicarbonyl leaders all contain 33 atoms and all improve despite Parent sizes of 34, 32 and 29; a contracted 32-atom relative remains close to its 33-atom leader. Different seed families show actual evaluated variation, but not the contents or exposure of unselected pools.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently retain productive functional-group context while avoiding unhelpful fragmentation or repeated scaffold expansion.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Use accepted task-local evidence to preserve useful aromatic, amine and carbonyl relationships during simplification, growth and chemically independent scaffold replacement. Evaluate whether new alternatives retain useful scores and plausible chemistry. Avoid a fixed size floor, automatic growth preference or an assumption that distinct native hash identifiers imply independent molecular scaffolds; the current evidence supports neither a pool-coverage claim nor a causal benefit for more diversity.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

retained_mechanisms: Score-quantile parent allocation, previously accepted scored parents, bounded greedy survival and the full accepted-score archive.
Connected-fragment crossover with unchanged post-crossover mutation probability and multi-parent opportunities.
Ordinary single-atom replacement plus append, delete, insert, bond-change, ring-open and ring-close mutations, with inherited walk and saturation laws.
Sanitization, stable canonical identity admission, initial/emitted and temporary-pool duplicate rejection, bounded retries and fixed surplus pools.

Native integer-count Morgan environments and exact generalized count-Tanimoto covariance; accepted-only chronological GP fitting, unchanged normalization/noise/jitter and full posterior covariance. Multiplicity is retained while fixed-width folding is removed only from active coordinates.
Correlated posterior score draws with masks, exact pool-to-emission predictions, pending identity joins and next-fit feedback probes.
Passive aromatic-pair enumeration and the unreachable direct-exchange implementation retained for controlled attribution.
Fresh objective-local state, deterministic prepared settings, ten-member announced batches and protocol-owned budgets/resources.
